Em Rio de Janeiro: Feijoada de sábado.
Order and enjoy Brazil’s national dish · In Rio, Saturday means feijoada: black beans with pork, served with rice, collard greens (“couve”), farofa and orange slices.
Em São Paulo: Receita de brigadeiro.
Follow a simple recipe step by step · Brigadeiro is Brazil’s chocolate truffle at every birthday.
Em Porto Alegre: Churrasco no domingo.
Join a barbecue and order meat · In the south, the churrasco is a ritual: meat on skewers (“espeto”), “picanha”, “linguiça”, and “farofa”.
Write a shopping list and cook dinner · In Curitiba, you cook dinner for friends: “arroz, feijão, frango, salada”.
Try street food in Bahia · In Salvador, the “baiana” sells acarajé, a fried bean fritter with shrimp and vatapá.
Em Belo Horizonte: Café da manhã brasileiro.
Describe a typical Brazilian breakfast · A typical breakfast in Minas Gerais: “pão de queijo”, “café”, “queijo minas”, “mamão”, “tapioca”.
Em São Paulo: Suco e lanche.
Order juice and a snack at a lanchonete · At a Brazilian “lanchonete” you pick juice (“suco de laranja, de maracujá, de caju”) and a snack (“coxinha, pastel, misto-quente”).
Explain food allergies and vegetarian choices · In Florianópolis, many people are vegetarian or lactose intolerant.
Em São Paulo: Jantar em família.
Join a family dinner and give compliments · A Sunday dinner with a Brazilian family means “macarrão”, “salada” and dessert.
